Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 4c04c6b47c361612b1d70cec8f7a60b1482d1400 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: SeongJae Park <sj@kernel.org>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 06:44:17 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] mm/damon/stat: deallocate damon_call() failure leaking
 damon_ctx
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

damon_stat_start() always allocates the module's damon_ctx object
(damon_stat_context).  Meanwhile, if damon_call() in the function fails,
the damon_ctx object is not deallocated.  Hence, if the damon_call() is
failed, and the user writes Y to “enabled” again, the previously
allocated damon_ctx object is leaked.

This cannot simply be fixed by deallocating the damon_ctx object when
damon_call() fails.  That's because damon_call() failure doesn't guarantee
the kdamond main function, which accesses the damon_ctx object, is
completely finished.  In other words, if damon_stat_start() deallocates
the damon_ctx object after damon_call() failure, the not-yet-terminated
kdamond could access the freed memory (use-after-free).

Fix the leak while avoiding the use-after-free by keeping returning
damon_stat_start() without deallocating the damon_ctx object after
damon_call() failure, but deallocating it when the function is invoked
again and the kdamond is completely terminated.  If the kdamond is not yet
terminated, simply return -EAGAIN, as the kdamond will soon be terminated.

The issue was discovered [1] by sashiko.

Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20260402134418.74121-1-sj@kernel.org
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/20260401012428.86694-1-sj@kernel.org [1]
Fixes: 405f61996d9d ("mm/damon/stat: use damon_call() repeat mode instead of damon_callback")
Signed-off-by: SeongJae Park <sj@kernel.org>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 6.17.x
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/mm/damon/stat.c b/mm/damon/stat.c
index cf2c5a541eee..60351a719460 100644
--- a/mm/damon/stat.c
+++ b/mm/damon/stat.c
@@ -245,6 +245,12 @@ static int damon_stat_start(void)
 {
 	int err;
 
+	if (damon_stat_context) {
+		if (damon_is_running(damon_stat_context))
+			return -EAGAIN;
+		damon_destroy_ctx(damon_stat_context);
+	}
+
 	damon_stat_context = damon_stat_build_ctx();
 	if (!damon_stat_context)
 		return -ENOMEM;
@@ -261,6 +267,7 @@ static void damon_stat_stop(void)
 {
 	damon_stop(&damon_stat_context, 1);
 	damon_destroy_ctx(damon_stat_context);
+	damon_stat_context = NULL;
 }
 
 static int damon_stat_enabled_store(
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

The patch fixes a memory leak in `mm/damon/stat.c` where a `damon_ctx` object is leaked when `damon_call()` fails in `damon_stat_start()`. The fix also avoids a potential use-after-free by ensuring the old context is only freed after its associated kdamond has fully terminated.

### Modifications in each file

- **File:** `mm/damon/stat.c`

  1. **`damon_stat_start()` function:**
     - Added a check before allocating a new `damon_stat_context`. If `damon_stat_context` is already non-NULL:
       - If the context is still running (`damon_is_running()`), return `-EAGAIN` – the caller should retry later.
       - If the context is no longer running, destroy it (`damon_destroy_ctx()`) to free the previously allocated (and leaked) object.
     - This ensures that a stale context leftover from a failed `damon_call()` is properly deallocated, and that no use-after-free occurs because termination is guaranteed.

  2. **`damon_stat_stop()` function:**
     - After destroying the context, set `damon_stat_context = NULL`. This prevents a dangling pointer that could cause double-free or other errors in subsequent calls to `damon_stat_start()`.

### Relationships between the modifications

- The change in `damon_stat_start()` directly addresses the leak by cleaning up any residual context from a prior failed start.
- The change in `damon_stat_stop()` complements this by correctly resetting the global pointer to NULL, ensuring that the cleanup logic in `damon_stat_start()` works correctly (i.e., it can detect that no context exists or that a leftover context is present).
- Together, the two modifications form a complete fix: the start function handles both the leak and the use-after-free risk, while the stop function maintains consistent state tracking.

Here is the commit message:
mm/damon/stat: deallocate damon_call() failure leaking
 damon_ctx
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

damon_stat_start() always allocates the module's damon_ctx object
(damon_stat_context).  Meanwhile, if damon_call() in the function fails,
the damon_ctx object is not deallocated.  Hence, if the damon_call() is
failed, and the user writes Y to “enabled” again, the previously
allocated damon_ctx object is leaked.

This cannot simply be fixed by deallocating the damon_ctx object when
damon_call() fails.  That's because damon_call() failure doesn't guarantee
the kdamond main function, which accesses the damon_ctx object, is
completely finished.  In other words, if damon_stat_start() deallocates
the damon_ctx object after damon_call() failure, the not-yet-terminated
kdamond could access the freed memory (use-after-free).

Fix the leak while avoiding the use-after-free by keeping returning
damon_stat_start() without deallocating the damon_ctx object after
damon_call() failure, but deallocating it when the function is invoked
again and the kdamond is completely terminated.  If the kdamond is not yet
terminated, simply return -EAGAIN, as the kdamond will soon be terminated.

The issue was discovered [1] by sashiko.

Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20260402134418.74121-1-sj@kernel.org
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/20260401012428.86694-1-sj@kernel.org [1]
Fixes: 405f61996d9d ("mm/damon/stat: use damon_call() repeat mode instead of damon_callback")
Signed-off-by: SeongJae Park <sj@kernel.org>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 6.17.x
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The function `damon_stat_start()` allocates a new `damon_ctx` object every time it is called without checking for a previously allocated context from a prior failed attempt (when `damon_call()` fails). The old context is not deallocated, leading to a memory leak. Additionally, `damon_stat_stop()` does not set `damon_stat_context` to `NULL` after destroying it, leaving a dangling pointer that can cause issues on subsequent calls. The fix addresses this by checking for an existing context at the start of `damon_stat_start()` and either returning `-EAGAIN` if still running or destroying it if fully terminated, and by resetting the pointer in the stop function.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int damon_stat_start(void)
 {
 	int err;
 
+	if (damon_stat_context) {
+		if (damon_is_running(damon_stat_context))
+			return -EAGAIN;
+		damon_destroy_ctx(damon_stat_context);
+	}
+
 	damon_stat_context = damon_stat_build_ctx();
 	if (!damon_stat_context)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 	err = damon_start(&damon_stat_context, 1, true);
 	if (err)
 		return err;
 
 	damon_stat_last_refresh_jiffies = jiffies;
 	call_control.data = damon_stat_context;
 	return damon_call(damon_stat_context, &call_control);
 }
 
 static void damon_stat_stop(void)
 {
 	damon_stop(&damon_stat_context, 1);
 	damon_destroy_ctx(damon_stat_context);
+	damon_stat_context = NULL;
 }
